abstracts.abstract: This paper introduces a novel theoretical framework for fuzzy set theory based on three-valued membership functions, fundamentally extending classical fuzzy logic to address higher-order uncertainty representation. Traditional fuzzy sets characterize uncertainty through a single membership degree in the interval [0,1], which often proves insufficient for modeling complex decision-making scenarios where uncertainty stems from multiple sources. The proposed framework introduces a triple membership structure comprising acceptance, hesitation, and rejection degrees, which collectively capture the multifaceted nature of uncertainty in human cognition. We establish a complete axiomatic system for these three-valued fuzzy sets, proving fundamental theorems including extension principles, decomposition theorems, and representation theorems that generalize classical fuzzy mathematics. The algebraic structure of three-valued fuzzy sets is investigated, revealing novel properties including non-commutative t-norms and enhanced fuzzy measures that do not exist in conventional fuzzy theory. Importantly, we demonstrate that classical fuzzy sets emerge as a special case when the hesitation degree vanishes, establishing a natural theoretical hierarchy. This paradigm shift provides mathematicians and practitioners with unprecedented tools for modeling uncertainty in fuzzy optimization, fuzzy decision making, and fuzzy topology applications where conventional approaches fail to adequately represent information granularity. The framework opens new research directions in fuzzy mathematics and soft computing.

This paper proposes a significantly enhanced fuzzy metric space theory that addresses critical limitations in existing distance measurement approaches for fuzzy sets. While classical fuzzy metrics provide foundational tools for analyzing fuzzy topological spaces, they often exhibit counterintuitive behavior when measuring distances between fuzzy sets with overlapping support regions. The proposed improved fuzzy metric incorporates a novel penalty function that accounts for both cardinality differences and shape dissimilarities between fuzzy sets, yielding more intuitively plausible distance assessments. We prove that the new metric satisfies all axiomatic requirements of a fuzzy metric space and demonstrate its convergence properties under various fuzzy set operations. The theoretical framework extends naturally to hesitant fuzzy environments, enabling distance computation in contexts where decision-makers express multiple possible values. A comprehensive comparison with existing fuzzy metrics reveals that the proposed approach achieves superior discrimination power while maintaining computational efficiency. The applications to fuzzy optimization and fuzzy decision making problems demonstrate that the improved metric enables more accurate ranking of alternatives in fuzzy multi-criteria decision analysis. The theoretical contributions advance fuzzy mathematics by providing practitioners with mathematically rigorous yet intuitively meaningful tools for fuzzy set comparison.

This paper introduces a novel evolvable interval type-2 fuzzy neural network architecture designed for autonomous control in complex dynamic systems with substantial parametric uncertainty. Conventional fuzzy control systems typically employ fixed rule bases and predefined membership functions that cannot adapt when system parameters change or novel operating conditions emerge. The proposed framework implements a dynamic self-organizing mechanism that enables the network topology to evolve autonomously based on real-time performance feedback, representing a fundamental departure from traditional fuzzy neural network designs. The system integrates interval type-2 fuzzy sets with neural network learning algorithms, achieving superior uncertainty quantification through footprint of uncertainty analysis that captures both linguistic and numerical ambiguities inherent in autonomous control scenarios. The evolution controller continuously monitors system performance metrics and triggers structural modifications including rule addition, rule merging, and parameter adaptation through a bio-inspired optimization process. Rigorous stability analysis using Lyapunov-based methods proves that the closed-loop adaptive system maintains uniform ultimate boundedness despite continuous structural evolution. Extensive simulation results in autonomous vehicle trajectory tracking demonstrate exceptional performance under severe sensor noise, actuator nonlinearities, and dynamically changing traffic scenarios, significantly outperforming existing adaptive and intelligent control methodologies.

This paper presents an enhanced type-2 fuzzy rule-based classification system integrating deep feature extraction for improved pattern recognition performance. Traditional fuzzy rule-based systems suffer from limited representation capacity when processing raw data, as they typically rely on hand-engineered features that may not capture discriminative patterns essential for accurate classification. The proposed methodology addresses this limitation by incorporating a pre-trained convolutional neural network as an intelligent feature extractor that generates high-level representations from raw input data. These deep features are then mapped to interval type-2 fuzzy membership functions, enabling the system to preserve and appropriately model the uncertainty arising from the feature extraction process itself. An optimized Mamdani-type fuzzy inference mechanism processes these uncertain features through interpretable fuzzy rules generated via a novel multi-objective clustering algorithm balancing classification accuracy and rule simplicity. The system maintains interpretability guarantees essential for explainable AI applications while achieving deep learning-level accuracy. Comprehensive experimental validation on benchmark datasets including medical diagnosis and industrial fault detection demonstrates substantial improvements in classification accuracy, robustness to noisy inputs, and uncertainty quantification capability compared to conventional type-1 fuzzy classifiers and standard neural network approaches. The methodology provides a practical framework for deploying interpretable fuzzy systems in complex real-world classification scenarios.
